study.setting: Netherlands Cancer Institute, head-and-neck oncology; April-June 2025.
study.population_or_dataset: Nine professionals: six clinicians plus three supervisors; real first consultations.

sample_sizes.reason: Complete questionnaire data; these are not 33 workload-independent participants.
Supplementary Figure 1; 43 intended for study preparation, 33 analysed.
Two of the 33 lacked a duration estimate.

study.comparator: Within-participant routine-work baseline, not a concurrent randomised control.
primary_endpoints: Perceived workflow usability/workload; outcome measures fixed before collection, without a preregistered statistical analysis plan.
secondary_exploratory_endpoints: Perceived time saving, preparation success, completeness and workload subscales.

results.locator: Results, Reduction in overall workload; Figure 1; Supplementary Table 1.

results.comparator: Self-estimated against usual preparation; not stopwatch measurement.
No concurrent control for this proportion.
results.uncertainty: Descriptive proportion; clustering-adjusted probability is a different estimate.
results.locator: Results, Effectiveness of AI in First Consultation Preparation, page 4.

study.follow_up: Eight-week study; clinicians assessed up to two clinic sessions. No patient-outcome follow-up evaluated.
study.harms: Four participant-reported discrepancy cases reviewed; two concern missing allergy data during downstream integration. No systematic safety ascertainment or incidence estimate.
study.analysis_notes: Repeated consultation ratings aggregated by professional for workload. Fixed sequence, different baseline referent and missing observations limit causal inference.
study.applicability: Local usability and pipeline observations; not an implementation-effectiveness or patient-benefit trial.

claims.supported_statement: Two reported cases converted missing allergy information into a negative statement during downstream EHR processing; original summaries retained an unknown state.
locators: Page 4, Table 1a, cases 1/2; Data analysis safety paragraph.
claims.evidence_scope: Observed handoff discrepancies, not demonstrated patient harm or an estimated error rate.
limitations: Spontaneous participant reports; no systematic audit of all outputs.

verification.checked_by: Codex (model evidence review; no independent human approval)
verification.supported_scope: Observed handoff discrepancies, not demonstrated patient harm or an estimated error rate.
verification.reason: Checked Page 4, Table 1a, cases 1/2; Data analysis safety paragraph. No extrapolation beyond the stated scope.

safety.report_type: Participant-reported discrepancies reviewed retrospectively within a prospective usability study.
safety.exposure_denominator: Unknown for ascertainment: 33 consultations analysed for usability, but not all summaries systematically audited.
safety.causality_limits: Report locates the wording change after generation; it does not establish patient injury or general product failure rates.
safety.duplicate_assessment: Table 1a explicitly identifies two separate occurrences of the same missing-versus-unknown allergy discrepancy.

rationales.significance: Concrete integration failure mode with practical evaluation consequences; no urgent withdrawal or quantified patient harm.
rationales.claim_support: Accepted manuscript, Table 1a and supplement directly support the bounded observation.
rationales.relevance: Directly relevant to European clinical AI integration teams.
rationales.material_change: Journal details add observed handoff discrepancies and completeness limitations beyond the earlier conference abstract.
rationales.durability: Missing-versus-negative semantics remain relevant across future integrations.

publication_verification.checked_by: Codex (model evidence review; no independent human approval)
publication_verification.supported_scope: Accepted manuscript and supplement support local usability and reported downstream discrepancies only; no causal patient-benefit, clinical-safety or incidence claim.
publication_verification.reason: Inspected the publisher-linked accepted manuscript and supplement, visually checked Table 1a, compared the earlier conference abstract and searched the DOI for notices. Use journal definitions; retain study limitations and source-access observations.

decision_history.reason: Select the bounded workflow and integration finding; its practical consequence is end-to-end validation, not clinical adoption approval.

evidence.publication_status: Peer-reviewed accepted manuscript; article in press, published 17 October 2026.
evidence.study_design: Prospective single-group pre/post usability evaluation; non-randomised.
evidence.validation_setting: One Dutch head-and-neck oncology department; six clinicians and three supervisors.
evidence.independent_validation: Developer-affiliated authors; primary analysis separated institutionally. No independent multisite replication established.
evidence.conflicts_of_interest: Three authors employed by kaiko.ai; one former employee. Institutional team performed primary outcome analysis; supplier-affiliated physician contributed to secondary discrepancy review.
evidence.corrections_retractions: No correction/retraction notice identified in inspected publisher records or targeted DOI search at extraction time; not continuous surveillance.
contradictory_findings: Earlier conference abstract reports 30.1% workload reduction and no observed hallucinations; journal report uses a different estimate and details downstream discrepancies. Use journal definitions and results; do not merge the estimates.
limitations: Single group, small sample and self-reported outcomes; baseline and follow-up refer to different measurement contexts.
33 analysed consultations from 72 eligible; incomplete capture may favour successful use.
No prespecified prospective safety endpoint or systematic review of every summary; discrepancy frequency cannot be estimated.
Proprietary implementation/prompts and restricted underlying data limit independent reproduction.
evidence.applicability: Early workflow evaluation in one specialised Dutch department. No demonstrated patient benefit, general safety claim, efficacy comparison or EU market-authorisation conclusion.
